syllabus_topics: Introduction to the Theory of machines and mechanisms. Introduction. Definition of machine, mechanism and kinematic chain. Members and kinematic pairs. Classification. Schematization, modeling and symbology. Mobility. Degrees of freedom. Synthesis of mechanisms.
Geometric analysis of mechanisms. Introduction. Methods for calculating position. Circuit closure equations.
Kinematic analysis of mechanisms. Fundamentals. Graphical methods. Analytical methods. Matrix methods.
Static analysis of mechanisms. Fundamentals. Force reduction. Virtual work/power method.
Dynamic analysis of mechanisms. Fundamentals. General dynamics of machines. Work and power in machines. Balancing dynamics.
Cam mechanisms. General fundamentals. Planar Cams. Cam synthesis.
Transmission mechanisms. Fundamentals. Gear mechanisms. Other mechanisms.
assessment_rules: The course is passed with a final grade equal to or greater than 5. The final grade is based on problem-solving tests (80%) and laboratory practices (20%). Minimum grades may be established for problem-solving tests, and minimum attendance for lab practices is required for evaluation. Students who renounce continuous evaluation will take a single comprehensive exam. Unethical behavior will result in a 0.0 final grade for the course.
